title: Pre-Purchase Ship Inspection Hong Kong | Buyers & Lessors
description: Pre-purchase inspection in Hong Kong for ship buyers, lessors and banks: condition and thickness readings at the anchorages, Kwai Tsing and Tsing Yi.
h1: Pre-Purchase Inspection for Ships Bought or Financed in Hong Kong
intro: Hong Kong is where many ship purchases are financed, structured and signed, even when the ship is trading far away. Buyers, lessors arranging sale-and-leaseback deals and banks lending against tonnage all need to know what they are taking on before the memorandum is final. When the ship comes into Hong Kong waters, the inspection is usually done at a designated anchorage during a bunker or crew stop, alongside at Kwai Tsing, or at a Tsing Yi repair yard. Atlantis sends its team from India to the ship, in Hong Kong or in the Delta yard where she is docking.

highlights.h: Evidence for lessors and banks too
highlights.p: A sale-and-leaseback makes the lessor the buyer, and a bank lending on a purchase takes the ship as security. Both need an independent account of her condition at the moment of purchase, written so that someone who never boards can rely on it.

Bulk carriers, tankers and gas carriers call at the designated anchorages for fuel, crew and stores between Chinese and Southeast Asian ports. In ballast and out of cargo work, they can open holds and tanks for a buyer's visit without deviating from the voyage.

highlights.h: Planned around typhoons and harbour traffic
highlights.p: From early summer into autumn, tropical cyclone signals can stop launch services and send ships out of the anchorages. A harbour crowded with ferries, barges and river craft also governs launch timing, so the plan carries a reserve day where the sale terms allow it.

sections.h: Where can a buyer inspect a ship in Hong Kong waters?
p: The designated anchorages give the most useful access. A ship stopping for bunkers, crew change, stores or orders is out of cargo operations, and if she is in ballast her holds and ballast tanks can be prepared for entry. The seller's agent books the launch and times it around harbour traffic, which in Hong Kong means a constant stream of ferries, barges and river trade craft as well as ships.

At the Kwai Tsing container terminals a container ship works cargo for the whole call, so a buyer's inspection there covers the deck, coaming tops, lashing areas, accommodation and engine room, with tanks entered only if the master can release them safely during the stay. Ships at the mid-stream buoys are busy with barges on both sides and suit little more than a records review and engine room readings. The Tsing Yi repair yards are the opposite: a ship under afloat repair may have tanks open and staging rigged, and the seller's repair list is itself worth reading.

If the ship is docking across the boundary in Shenzhen or elsewhere in the Pearl River Delta, the buyer may prefer to see her there, dry. That needs a Chinese visa for the team as well as Hong Kong entry, and the earlier it is known, the better.
list: Designated anchorages: holds, ballast tanks, deck and machinery on ships stopping for fuel, crew or orders
Kwai Tsing Container Terminals: deck, coamings, lashing areas and engine room during the working call
Mid-stream buoys: records review and machinery readings, with deck access as cargo work allows
Tsing Yi repair yards: wider access during afloat repairs, with the seller's repair list on hand
Delta yards across the boundary: dry-docked ships, with Chinese visas arranged for the team

sections.h: Who commissions a pre-purchase inspection from Hong Kong?
p: Hong Kong ship managers buy for owners worldwide, and the ship they are buying is often in another port entirely; the inspection is then mobilised to wherever she is, and the report is laid out for a technical team that may run a large fleet. Hong Kong owners buying tonnage for their own fleets ask for the same thing in Hong Kong waters when the ship calls there.

Lessors are the other large group. Hong Kong has offered tax concessions to qualifying ship lessors since 2020, and sale-and-leaseback finance, in which the lessor buys a ship from her owner and charters her straight back, needs a record of condition at the start. Banks lending against a purchase want something similar before drawdown. For these readers the inspection is less about the negotiation than about the security: what state the ship was in when ownership changed.

Smaller craft change hands too. River trade vessels, barges and harbour craft working between Hong Kong and the Pearl River ports are bought and sold locally, and a buyer can have their hulls, tanks and machinery checked during a lay-by between jobs.

sections.h: How is a buyer's inspection scoped on a Hong Kong anchorage call?
p: Ships stop briefly in Hong Kong, so the scope is set by what the call is for. A bulk carrier bunkering in ballast can usually open some of her holds and ballast tanks; a laden container ship cannot open holds at all; a gas carrier's cargo tanks are never entered, so that visit concentrates on ballast spaces, deck structure around the tank domes and machinery.

Machinery readings depend on what is running at anchor. Generators, ballast pumps, compressors and fans can be read with the chief engineer; on a gas carrier, the cargo compressors and reliquefaction plant are included only if they are in service and the master agrees. Records are read on board, and anything missing is noted for the broker to request from the seller.

A ship under the Hong Kong flag may have been through a flag state inspection by the Marine Department, and every foreign ship calling here is liable to port state control under the Tokyo MoU, of which Hong Kong is a member in its own right. Those results are worth reading before boarding, because recurring structural or fire-main items point the team to the places to measure first.

sections.h: Typhoon season, harbour traffic and the inspection window
p: Tropical cyclones shape the Hong Kong calendar from early summer to autumn. When a signal is raised, launch services stop, anchorage work ends and ships may leave the harbour to ride out the weather, so an inspection booked for that day is lost. Where the sale terms give a fixed inspection period, it helps to ask the brokers for some flexibility or to plan the visit early in the ship's stay.

Even on calm days the harbour is crowded. Launch transfers are timed around ferry lanes and traffic, and boarding at a busy anchorage can take longer than the distance suggests. The plan therefore sets out the order in which spaces are taken, so that a late start drops the least important items rather than the ballast tanks the buyer most wants to see.

sections.h: What does the report show a buyer, a lessor or a bank?
p: For a buyer, the report sorts findings by their weight in the negotiation and at the next survey: hold and tank wastage near renewal limits, coating breakdown in ballast spaces, hatch cover wear, cracks at fatigue details, and machinery readings out of line with sister units. For a lessor or bank, the same findings are presented as a condition record dated to the purchase, with every reading located and every photograph tied to a space, so the document can stand on its own years later when the ship is returned or the loan is reviewed.

Either way, the report states what it is not. It is not a class survey and gives no view on the deal. Thickness readings taken for a buyer are evidence for the buyer's decision only; class credits readings solely from firms holding IACS UR Z17 approval from the ship's own society, and Atlantis is in the process of obtaining UR Z17 approval from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS.

sections.h: Worked scope: a Supramax in a sale-and-leaseback, at a Hong Kong anchorage
p: Picture a Supramax bulk carrier in her early teens being sold to a lessor and chartered back to her current owner, calling at a Hong Kong anchorage for bunkers in ballast. The lessor's brief is a dated condition record rather than points for the negotiation, so the plan covers every hold that can be prepared, a spread of ballast tanks along the length, hatch covers and coamings, deck plating and the engine room.

Holds are inspected for frame and bracket condition and grab damage, with spot readings on hopper and lower bulkhead plating; ballast tanks are rated for coating and gauged at the bottom and the upper parts; hatch covers are checked for packing, cleats and drainage. In the engine room, the generators and pumps are read while running. The report is addressed to the lessor and the bank together, as agreed beforehand, and lists the holds and tanks that could not be opened during the stop.

codes: Norwegian Saleform (NSF 2012) Clause 4 – the buyers' right to inspect
IACS UR Z10.2 – hull surveys of bulk carriers
IACS UR Z7 – hull classification surveys and coating condition terms
IGC Code – construction and equipment of ships carrying liquefied gases in bulk
ASTM E797 – manual pulse-echo ultrasonic thickness measurement
ISO 20816-1 – measurement and evaluation of machine vibration
deliverables: Condition record dated to the transaction, addressed as the client directs
Hold, tank and deck findings with coating ratings and located photographs
Spot thickness readings compared with as-built or previous class readings
Hatch cover and crack-check findings at fatigue details
Machinery vibration and thermal readings with the operating condition
Spaces not opened during the call, with the reason for each

faqs.q: Can a pre-purchase inspection be done at a Hong Kong anchorage?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships stopping at the designated anchorages for bunkers, crew change, stores or orders are the usual subjects, because they are out of cargo work and, in ballast, can open holds and tanks. The seller's agent books the launch. Tell us how long she will stay and what she is doing there, and the scope is set to fit that window.

faqs.q: What happens if a typhoon signal goes up during the inspection?
faqs.a: Work stops when launch services are suspended, and the ship may leave the anchorage to ride out the weather. The team resumes when it is safe and the ship is accessible again, if the sale terms leave time. Where the inspection period is fixed and short, it is worth asking the brokers for room to move the visit before the season makes the choice for you.

faqs.q: Can you inspect a ship docking in Shenzhen or Guangdong for a Hong Kong buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Hong Kong buyers prefer to see the ship dry in a Delta yard, where the bottom shell, sea chests and stern area can be examined. The team needs a Chinese visa as well as Hong Kong entry, and the Chinese visa takes longer, so send the yard and the docking window to info@atlantisndt.com as early as possible.

faqs.q: Is the report suitable for a sale-and-leaseback lessor or a lending bank?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is commissioned with that purpose in mind. The report can be addressed to the lessor and the financing bank together and written as a condition record dated to the transaction. If the lessor uses a standard condition template, send it before the visit so the findings follow its layout. The scope does not change with the addressee.

faqs.q: Can a container ship be inspected at Kwai Tsing while she works cargo?
faqs.a: Partly. Cargo stays on board and the cranes keep working, so the visit covers the open deck, hatch coaming tops, lashing areas, accommodation and engine room, plus any ballast tank the master can release safely. Holds cannot be entered. For a fuller look before the memorandum is final, an anchorage stop or a repair yard period is the better choice.

faqs.q: Do you inspect river trade vessels and barges before purchase?
faqs.a: Yes. River trade vessels and barges working between Hong Kong and the Pearl River ports change hands locally, and the same approach applies: hull and deck condition, spot readings, tanks where they can be opened safely, and machinery readings with the engines running. These craft rarely stop for long, so ask the seller for a lay-by period between jobs.
